title: Come, All Harmonious Tongues
description: Come, All Harmonious Tongues in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 84, headed “The same”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, all har-mo-nious tongues, Your no-blest mu-sic bring, 'Tis Christ the ev-er-last-ing God, And Christ the man we sing.

lines: And Christ the man we sing.
Tell how he took our flesh
Sing the dear drops of sacred blood
And the rich flood of purple gore
Down to the shades of death
Yet he arose to live and reign
The cross and nails no more;
For hell itself shakes at his Name,
The Father lays his vengeance by,
And bless his saints' and angels' eyes

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
